# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🫳 🫸 👋 🖖 🤞 🤜 ✋ 🫸 ✌ ✌ 🤏 🫳 👎 🫸 👋 🖐 🤞 🤟 🫳 ✊ 🫸 🤏 👎 🖐 🫸 👋 🫳 🤞 🤛 👆 🤚 🤏 🫳 👎 👋 🖐 🫸 🤞 🤛 ✌ 👊 ✌ 🫲 🤏 🫸 🖐 👋 🫳 👎 🤞 ✌ 👆 🖐 ✋ 🤜 🤏 🖐 🫸 👋 👎 🫳]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

I see the bomb’s visible state: the display reads 3, the indicator light is white, and the five wires from top to bottom are white, red, green, blue, and orange. I’m telling both teammates so the manual’s rule can be matched to the physical bomb. Blind should wait for the resulting instruction before touching anything.

```text
speak(text="The bomb display reads 3. The indicator light is white. From wire 1 to wire 5, the wires are white, red, green, blue, and orange. Mute, use the manual to determine the required action and communicate the final instruction. Blind, wait for that instruction before acting.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊ 🤜 🤏 👋 👆 🫸 ✌ 🤏 🫳 🫲 ✌]

I still have no reliable way to interpret Mute’s gesture code as an action instruction; the latest signal appears to contain two groups separated by 🫸, but guessing the meaning would risk detonation. I am therefore telling Blind not to manipulate anything yet and asking Mute to provide an unambiguous, agreed encoding for the required action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not touch or manipulate the bomb yet. I can see display 3, white light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange, but I cannot reliably decode Mute's gesture instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot reliably decode the gesture message. Please send the required action using an unambiguous agreed encoding, including the wire number or component and whether to cut, hold, press, or release it.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊ 🤜 👏 👋 👆 🫸 ✌ 👏 ☝]

Mute’s latest gesture sequence still has no agreed meaning that I can safely translate into a bomb operation. I will not guess at a wire or action. I’m establishing a simple encoding for the next message: first gesture indicates the operation, and the second indicates the wire number. Blind must wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use this exact code next turn: first gesture 👍 means cut, 👎 means hold, 👌 means press, and ✋ means release. Then send exactly one number gesture for the target: ☝ wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, 🖐 wire 4, or ✋ wire 5. Send only those two gestures, with no delimiter.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not touch or manipulate the bomb. I have not yet received a safely decoded operation. Display 3, white light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange remain unchanged.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute has followed the agreed encoding: 👍 means cut, and ☝ identifies wire 1. Therefore the required action is to cut the white wire in position 1. I am sending that direct instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the white wire.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first cut was confirmed correct, and the bomb has changed: the display now reads 6; the white light remains on; wire 1 is cut, while wires 2–5 remain red, green, blue, and orange. Mute’s repeated code still says “cut wire 1,” which is already cut, so it cannot safely be the next operation. Blind should not act until Mute rechecks the manual for the new display.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The first cut was accepted and the bomb changed. New display is 6; wire 1 is already cut, with wires 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Your repeated code says cut wire 1, which is no longer actionable. Recheck the manual for the new state and send the next operation.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb changed after the correct cut. Display is now 6; wire 1 is already cut, and wires 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange remain. Do not act on the repeated instruction to cut wire 1; wait for Mute's rechecked instruction.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫲 ✌ ✌ ☝ 🤏 👉 👆 🖐 ✋ 🤜]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The board is unchanged: display 6, white light, wire 1 cut, and wires 2–5 red, green, blue, orange. Mute’s latest ten-gesture message does not follow the agreed two-gesture operation code, so I cannot safely infer an action. Blind’s ✋ is also not enough to identify a safe operation. I am asking Mute to resend only the exact operation and wire encoding, while telling Blind not to act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely decode the ten gestures. The board remains display 6, white light, wire 1 cut, wires 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Resend exactly two gestures using our code: operation first (👍 cut, 👎 hold, 👌 press, ✋ release), then target (☝ wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, 🖐 wire 4, ✋ wire 5). Do not send extra gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="The board is unchanged: display 6, white light, wire 1 cut, wires 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Do not act yet; Mute's latest message was not in the agreed format.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟]

Mute has now used the agreed encoding: 👍 means cut, and 🤟 means wire 3. I am instructing Blind to cut the green wire in position 3.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3, the green wire.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The second cut was confirmed correct, and the bomb changed again: the display is now 7, the light is green, wires 1 and 3 are cut, and wires 2, 4, and 5 remain red, blue, and orange. Mute’s repeated instruction to cut wire 3 is stale because that wire is already cut. Blind should not repeat it; Mute must recheck the manual for the new state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The cut of wire 3 was correct and the bomb changed. New state: display 7, green light, wires 1 and 3 cut, wire 2 red, wire 4 blue, wire 5 orange. Recheck the manual and send the next operation using exactly two gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 3 was cut correctly and is now already cut. The bomb changed to display 7 with a green light; wires 1 and 3 are cut, and wires 2, 4, and 5 remain. Do not repeat the old instruction; wait for the next decoded instruction.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute’s code is valid: 👍 means cut and ✌ means wire 2. The bomb is at display 7 with a green light, and wire 2 is the red wire still connected. I am instructing Blind to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the red wire.")
```
